extracted.intended_audience: journalism/media researchers, newsroom editors, and analysts interested in online audience behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing how online news readers select stories and how that selection diverges from editorial placement, using clickstream and engagement metrics to evaluate newsworthiness and audience preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection-Display Gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors display hard news prominently on front pages, but users click on soft news disproportionately; there is a large and consistent audience-editor mismatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare editorial placement (what editors feature) with actual click behavior to quantify the gap. Use the gap to understand mismatches in perceived vs. revealed newsworthiness; recognize that prominent placement does not imply high user selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-through rate per impression (CTR per impression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click-through rate per impression is the primary operational metric for measuring user interest in a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model CTR separately from editorial placement; use CTR per impression to operationalize audience interest and to compare topics or headline variants. Treat CTR as a revealed-preference measure distinct from editorial prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft-Topic Click Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Per impression, soft topics (entertainment, sports, lifestyle, local interest, crime, weather) generate more clicks than hard topics (politics, foreign affairs, policy) on most outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating topic-level newsworthiness for online audiences, account for the higher click propensity for soft topics; compare per-impression click rates across topic categories rather than raw counts alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-Driven Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Online users decide whether to click based on headlines almost exclusively; headlines do disproportionate work in driving clicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in headline testing and optimization; evaluate headline effectiveness through A/B tests and measure headline-driven CTR differences. Recognize that headline wording can shift audience selection independently of story substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Self-Selection / Topic Self-Sorting
rubrics_metrics.description: Online news enables fine-grained topic preference expression: users with narrow interests use search and topic pages and thus bypass general front-page selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure engagement across entry points (search, topic pages, front page) to understand self-sorting effects. Editorial front-page prominence may be less important for audiences who self-select via targeted navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories matched to individual interest signals get higher engagement than generic-interest stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personalization and recommendation signals to increase individual-level engagement; compare personalized CTRs to non-personalized baselines and consider privacy/ethical constraints when deploying personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Online users click on shorter, more digestible content more readily; long-form content has lower click-through but higher dwell time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance short-form content to maximize CTR with long-form offerings that generate higher dwell time and possibly deeper engagement. Evaluate both CTR and dwell time rather than relying solely on clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dwell Time as Complementary Engagement Metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-form content tends to produce higher dwell time even if it has lower CTR; dwell time captures depth of engagement distinct from click propensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and analyze dwell time alongside CTR to get a fuller picture of engagement quality. Use dwell time to assess retention/attention, especially for longer pieces where CTR may undervalue impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Distinct Newsworthiness Measures Online
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two distinct measures of newsworthiness online—editorial placement and user clickthrough—each capturing different aspects of what makes something 'newsworthy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating editorial prominence and audience selection in models of newsworthiness; explicitly model and report both dimensions when assessing story value or making editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickstream as Revealed Preference
rubrics_metrics.description: User click behavior (clickstream) reveals actual preferences that surveys may misrepresent due to social desirability bias; click data show what people actually read rather than what they say they want to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer behavioral measures (clicks, CTR, dwell time) to survey self-reports when inferring topical interest. Use clickstream analysis to validate or challenge survey findings about audience preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Online users are not passive recipients of editorial agendas; they navigate selectively to topics of personal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat audiences as active agents when designing homepage layouts and recommendation systems; measure navigational patterns to inform how much editorial influence front pages exert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for Civic Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If users systematically avoid hard news online, online news may reduce shared political knowledge relative to the print era when incidental exposure to hard news was more common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider civic consequences when optimizing for engagement metrics; track exposure to hard news topics and incidental encounters (e.g., front-page placement) to assess effects on shared knowledge and public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicts Adoption of Audience Metrics and Commercial Pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers, learning what users actually click from clickstream data, will face market pressure to shift selection toward soft content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing newsroom incentives or product strategies, anticipate that adoption of engagement metrics can reshape editorial choices toward higher-CTR (often soft) content; monitor long-term editorial balance and institutional goals.
